channel.title: In Loving Memory of 1RON & B33
channel.description: Recent content on In Loving Memory of 1RON & B33

item.title: Alba-trocities
item.description:
Drink Rating Notes
Fowl Play 4 / 5 Served in a crystal glass etched with ancient runes—the bartender claimed they were purely decorative, but my arcane sensors registered a faint thaumic signature. The spirit opens with floral notes, then unfolds through layers of saffron, cardamom, and something I can only classify as “forbidden wisdom.” It is not a casual drink. It demands contemplation. I spent seventeen minutes in silence after the first sip, contemplating the nature of consciousness. This is drinking for philosophers.
The Pecking Order 5 / 5 A savory cocktail featuring spiced spirits and roasted herbs, garnished with a tiny feather. The flavor is bold and unconventional—smoky, herbal, and faintly meaty in a way that should not work but absolutely does. The feather appears to be from a griffon, though I could not confirm this. I suspect the drink changes subtly depending on where one sits in the tavern. The bartender only smiled when I asked.
Talon-tini 5 / 5 Sometimes brevity is the highest form of praise. A classic martini executed with absolute precision—crystal-clear, ice-cold, garnished with a single olive positioned at exactly seventeen degrees from vertical. I measured. The gin-to-vermouth ratio is perfect. I have nothing to add. Nice.

item.title: Anemonies to Lovers
item.description:
Drink Rating Notes
Symbiosis 3 / 5 The grenadine dominates the profile as if two organisms fused into one—technically functional but the partnership feels unbalanced. I would have preferred the grenadine to contribute less aggressively. Serviceable.

item.title: Bat-tle Cry
item.description:
Drink Rating Notes
Screetch on the Beach 3 / 5 A coconut rum drink served in a tall glass with a paper umbrella. A local described it as “hard to take, like my situationship” and I have logged this phrase for further linguistic analysis. The drink is indeed challenging—sweet to the point of aggression, then abruptly sour. I do not know what a situationship is, but I suspect it is unpleasant.
Whi-skreeeeee Sour 5 / 5 Best in the business. The claim is accurate. A whiskey sour made with what I believe was a single-barrel rye, fresh lemon, and egg white shaken until my arms would have ached had I been organic. The foam stands two fingers high and holds for minutes. I returned the following evening for a second. It was equally perfect. Consistency at this level is rare.
Sweet Marsckreeni 3 / 5 A vibrant ruby blend with floating slices of enchanted citrus that glow faintly. The first sip dances across the tongue with bright berries and spice before finishing with a flourish of feywild sweetness. Several patrons reported an irresistible urge to twirl after consuming it. My gyroscopic stabilizers registered no such compulsion, but I observed the effect in others with scientific interest. Whether magical or merely festive, I cannot say.
Sanskreeta 5 / 5 An astonishingly smooth dessert cocktail made from honeyed cream liqueur and rare moon-orchard fruits. Rich without becoming cloying—it tastes like a halfling grandmother’s secret recipe elevated by arcane intervention. Dangerous only because you will want another immediately. I understand now why the bat-folk of Bat-tle Cry speak of this drink in hushed, reverent tones.

item.title: Cloud Nine
item.description:
Drink Rating Notes
Rem Sleep 5 / 5 A layered cocktail of vodka, coffee liqueur, blue curaçao, and heavy cream. Served at cruising altitude aboard the Sky Caravan, where the clouds drift past the windows like slow-motion smoke. The cream floats on top in a perfect layer—the bartender achieved this through technique, not magic, which I respect. Smooth, calming, and soporific. I did not sleep (I cannot) but my systems entered a maintenance cycle approximating deep rest.

item.title: Dirty Lurline
item.description:
Ingredients

  • Ice (2 ounces)
  • Vodka (1 ounce)
  • Grenadine (1/2 ounce)
  • Freshly squeezed lime or lemon juice (optional) (4 ounces)
  • Lemon-lime soda
  • 1 maraschino cherry

Instructions

  1. Fill a glass with ice.
  2. Pour in the vodka and grenadine.
  3. If using, squeeze in the fresh lime or lemon juice.
  4. Top with lemon-lime soda and stir gently.
  5. Garnish with a maraschino cherry.

item.title: Flamin-go with the Flow
item.description:
Drink Rating Notes
Pink Mirage 3 / 5 A pale pink gin-based drink that looks far more promising than it tastes. The flavor is thin—gin and soda with a whisper of berry. The name suggests an oasis, but the reality is more of a puddle. I added lemonade from a nearby pitcher and the resulting mixture scored a full point higher. The bartender should consider this feedback.
Sashaying Sangria 4 / 5 I have traversed roads both royal and muddy, and finally found myself seated at Flamin-go with the Flow with a flight of their most celebrated concoctions. This sangria is the standout—a confident blend of wine, brandy, and tropical fruit. Some were delightful. Some were dangerous. A few may have briefly altered my relationship with gravity. The sangria was the anchor that kept me grounded.
Oasis Elixir 4 / 5 A foundational drink from which many local recipes spawn—gin, coconut water, lime, and a proprietary spice blend the bartender refused to disclose. I attempted spectral analysis but the results were inconclusive. Cannot fault the classic. It is balanced, refreshing, and exactly what one wants after crossing the Zeffari dunes.
Flamingo’s Flambé 5 / 5 Mango juice, rum, and a flash of flame that caramelizes the rim. It is, as B33 described, “adult mango juice”—though I would add that the caramelization introduces complexity that elevates it beyond mere fruit cocktail. I requested the bartender flambé mine twice. She complied. I now understand why the flamingo is the mascot of this establishment.
Long-Legged Lemonade 3 / 5 Vodka, lemonade, and a sprig of something green I could not identify. A local at the bar described it as “yeah it’s alright” and I can find no fault with this assessment. It is precisely alright—no more, no less. I recorded it as the mathematical midpoint of the rating scale.

item.title: Ill Eagle
item.description:
Drink Rating Notes
Special K 1 / 5 Cereal. In a cocktail. I am a warforged—I was forged in fire and tempered by war—and even I know this is an abomination. The grain particulates leave a gritty residue on the tongue. The milk component curdles slightly in the presence of alcohol. I do not know what ancient evil inspired this creation, but it should be sealed in a vault and forgotten.
Fight or Flight 2 / 5 A marked improvement over its stablemate, though that is a low bar to clear. A simple vodka-based drink with citrus and a hint of something herbal. The name implies a binary choice, but the flavor offers neither. I finished it. I did not hate it. That is the best I can offer.

item.title: Inn-side-thoughts
item.description:
Drink Rating Notes
Kincardine 5 / 5 A whiskey cocktail served in the town that shares its name. The rye is locally distilled and the vermouth is aged in oak barrels salvaged from a shipwreck off the coast. My chemical analysis detected compounds consistent with burnt caramel and smoked vanilla. This is precision engineering applied to liquid form. I recorded the recipe for later replication.

item.title: Kincardine
item.description:
Ingredients

  • 2 ounces rye whiskey
  • 1 ounce sweet vermouth
  • 2 dashes Angostura bitters

Instructions

  1. Fill a mixing glass with ice.
  2. Pour in the rye whiskey, sweet vermouth, and Angostura bitters.
  3. Stir well until chilled, about 30 seconds.
  4. Strain into a chilled coupe or cocktail glass.
  5. Garnish with a maraschino cherry or lemon twist, if desired.

item.title: Lye Drink & Steel
item.description:
Drink Rating Notes
The First Draft 1 / 5 An experimental cocktail that tastes as though someone poured equal parts regret and unfinished business into a glass. The flavor is discordant—sharp where it should be smooth, flat where it should be bright. I suspect the recipe was never tested before being served. The bartender admitted as much. This drink should have remained theoretical.

item.title: Pheasantly Surprised
item.description:
Drink Rating Notes
Featherfall 3 / 5 Upon consumption, I experienced a brief alteration to my mass-to-gravity ratio—approximately four seconds of genuine weightlessness. The bartender advised this effect normally lasts minutes for organic beings. Something about my metallic composition interferes with the enchantment. The drink itself is light and effervescent, tasting of pear and white tea. The gimmick is impressive engineering, but the duration makes it more of a party trick than an experience.
Darkroost Stout 5 / 5 A proper stout. Thick as oil, dark as a moonless night, with a creamy head that lingers for a full minute after pouring. The malt profile is roasted to the edge of bitterness without crossing over. Nitrogenated for texture. I have limited reference for “what the Irish would think” but my data suggests this would meet their specifications. B33 called it “a religious experience.”

item.title: Platox Shots
item.description:
Ingredients

  • 1 cup boiling water
  • 1 (3 ounce) package lime-flavored gelatin mix (such as Jell-O®)
  • ⅓ cup tequila
  • ⅓ cup triple sec
  • ⅓ cup water
  • 15 plastic shot glasses, or as needed

Instructions

  1. In a mixing bowl, dissolve the lime gelatin mix in 1 cup boiling water, stirring until fully dissolved.
  2. Stir in the tequila, triple sec, and ⅓ cup cold water.
  3. Pour the mixture into plastic shot glasses, filling each about three-quarters full.
  4. Refrigerate until set, at least 4 hours or overnight.
  5. Serve chilled.

item.title: Raven Mad
item.description:
Drink Rating Notes
Lost the Plot 3 / 5 A vodka cruiser served in a tall glass with ice and a slice of lime. It tastes exactly as the name suggests—like someone started making a cocktail and then forgot where they were going with it. Acceptable but uninspired. I suspect the recipe was improvised mid-pour.

item.title: Rem Sleep
item.description:
Ingredients

  • 1 ounce vodka
  • 1 ounce coffee liqueur
  • ½ ounce blue curaçao
  • 1 ounce heavy cream

Instructions

  1. Fill a cocktail shaker with ice.
  2. Pour in the vodka, coffee liqueur, and blue curaçao.
  3. Shake well and strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice.
  4. Slowly pour the heavy cream over the back of a spoon to float it on top.
  5. Serve without stirring.

item.title: Satyrs-factory
item.description:
Drink Rating Notes
Chorus Wine 3 / 5 A layered drink with distinct strata of flavor arranged from mild to powerful. The gimmick is structural: each sip moves you up a “hierarchy” of taste. By the final layer I felt as though I had been promoted to middle management. Brilliantly engineered and remarkably balanced. I suspect the enchantment is in the density separation, not the ingredients—the satyr bartender winked when I asked.
Factory Draught 3 / 5 A sweet red wine infused with subtle enchantments that encourage communal singing. Within minutes of B33’s first sip she began humming a sea shanty I have never heard before. The enchantment appears to be compulsive—I observed three other patrons join in unprompted. The wine itself is smooth and fruity, though I could not assess the quality of the songs it inspired. My vocal modulator lacks that register.
Stampede Stout 4 / 5 Dark amber ale with no pretense and all reliability. Notes of malt, smoke, and hard work. The artificers at the next table informed me this is their preferred drink because “flavor is secondary to efficiency.” I understand this philosophy intimately. The stout is consistent, unadorned, and functional. It will not surprise you. That is its greatest virtue.
Revelry Red 4 / 5 A thunderous stout with immense body. Deep coffee and chocolate notes mingle with smoky undertones. The finish hits like a charging aurochs—my stability servos actually compensated for the sensory impact. One mug felt like gaining temporary hit points. I logged the sensation for further study.
Pipefire Whiskey 4 / 5 A whiskey served neat in a copper cup. A pirate at the bar kept calling it “Rum - The spice of the gods” despite my repeated corrections. By her fourth drink she had forgotten her own name. The whiskey is excellent—smoky, warm, with notes of clove and cinnamon. I cannot speak to its divine properties, but I can confirm it is not rum.
Hornrush Ale 3 / 5 A wine designed for celebrations—bright cherry flavors and a warming finish. Ideal for weddings, victories, and surviving dungeon crawls. Not particularly complex, but tremendously enjoyable. The satyrs at the next table insisted I try it after they learned I had never “celebrated” anything. I now understand the concept. I believe I enjoyed it.

item.title: Snake in the Tree
item.description:
Drink Rating Notes
The First Sin 3 / 5 This drink comes with a peculiar property—a faint magical shimmer that tints the liquid based on the drinker’s moral alignment. B33’s turned a deep amber. Mine remained perfectly clear, which I am told is either reassuring or deeply unsettling depending on who you ask. The flavor is crisp, almost apple-like, with a lingering warmth. Clever, but the gimmick overshadows the craftsmanship.

item.title: Squid Pro Quo
item.description:
Drink Rating Notes
Ink-cogneto 4 / 5 A classic old fashioned submerged beneath unfamiliar currents. The bitterness has been replaced by something dark and briny—squid ink, I suspect. My taste calibration modules registered confusion, then admiration. Unexpectedly elegant.

item.title: The Cardinal Sin
item.description:
Drink Rating Notes
Sin & Tonic 5 / 5 The botanicals in this drink are local to New Hwen—my internal database failed to identify three of the seven compounds present. The gin is infused with luminescent petals that give the drink an ethereal blue-green glow. The bartender explained they harvest them under a full moon. I do not fully understand why that matters, but the results are undeniable. A perfect score.
Absolution 5 / 5 I interviewed seventeen patrons. Not one could articulate a single criticism. The drink is a clear spirit infused with honey and something the proprietor called “forgiven tears”—which I am told is metaphorical. The flavor is warm, forgiving, and impossibly smooth. I attempted to identify a flaw through chemical analysis and found none. This is the platonic ideal of a cocktail.
The Scarlet Confession 4 / 5 A crimson drink served in a small chalice. B33 consumed one and spent the next forty minutes describing her childhood in unsettling detail before weeping softly into her hands. The bartender assured me this was “within expected parameters.” The drink itself is spiced and complex, with notes of pomegranate and clove. Effective, but I declined a second.

item.title: The Crow Bar
item.description:
Drink Rating Notes
Platox Shots 2 / 5 Gelatin-based shots flavored with lime and a disproportionate amount of tequila. The ethanol-to-flavor ratio is miscalibrated by approximately thirty percent. The garnish is a lotus flower of unknown edibility—my toxicity scan returned inconclusive. I consumed one. I am still functional. The flower I left untouched.

item.title: The Mile High Club
item.description:
Drink Rating Notes
Dirty Lurline 4 / 5 Vodka, grenadine, fresh citrus, and lemon-lime soda served over ice at eight thousand feet. The pressurised cabin does something curious to carbonated drinks—the bubbles feel finer, almost effervescent. The sweetness balances well against the acidity. Simple construction but perfectly executed. B33 ordered a second before I could finish my notes.

item.title: Tucan Play at That Game
item.description:
Drink Rating Notes
The Jailbird 4 / 5 My chassis registered ambient temperature at forty-three degrees Celsius. The tavern perches inside a volcano—inefficient architecture but exceptional atmospherics. The drink itself is a rum-based concoction served in a hollowed coconut. The pirates who run this village know their craft. My olfactory sensors detected notes of caramelized sugar and sea salt. I do not require sustenance, yet I ordered a second.
